newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spy had shrewd investments.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spy had shrewd investments.

text.p: Where does a spy put his ill-gotten loot?
In the case of Harold James Nicholson, the former CIA case officer who pleaded guilty and is in jail awaiting sentencing for spying for Russia, he invested it.

The U.S. Attorney's office in Alexandria, Va., confirmed that a foreiture order was filed with the U.S. District Court there on Wednesday that listed what he did with $300,000 he got for passing papers to the Russians.

His investments, the Washington Post said, went into The Kaufman Fund, USAA's International Fund and its World Growth Fund. Also money went to Templeton Developing Markets Trust and Franklin Convertible Securities Fund.

The report noted he had a secret bank account in Switzerland and had eight gold coins, a Rolex watch, a stamp collection, five guns and a leather-bound collection of novels of Louis L'Amour, the late Western writer.
